reference.title: Histologic type (WHO 5th edition)
reference.intro: All non-endometrioid carcinomas are high grade by definition and take no FIGO grade. Confirm the type with the minimum immunohistochemistry needed; molecular class does not replace histotype.

groups.heading: Endometrioid carcinoma
points: Glands resembling proliferative endometrium, confluent or cribriform, often villoglandular
Squamous, mucinous, secretory or ciliated differentiation may be present
ER / PR positive, wild-type p53 in most; PTEN loss common
Distinguish from: serous (marked atypia, slit-like spaces, abnormal p53) and clear cell carcinoma

images.caption: Endometrioid: confluent glands, columnar cells, smooth luminal borders (40x)
Endometrioid with villoglandular pattern: slender papillae lined by low-grade columnar cells

groups.heading: Serous carcinoma
points: Complex papillae with cellular budding and slit-like glandular spaces; scalloped luminal borders
Marked nuclear atypia and pleomorphism, hobnail cells, macronucleoli, brisk mitoses, cherry-red nucleoli
Abnormal p53 (overexpression or null), diffuse p16, ER often reduced or lost; may arise in a polyp or as serous EIC
Distinguish from: FIGO grade 3 endometrioid and villoglandular endometrioid (bland nuclei, wild-type p53)

images.caption: Serous: discohesive, budding tumour cells with marked pleomorphism around fibrovascular cores
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, single image

images.caption: Serous carcinoma arising in an atrophic endometrial polyp
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, single image

images.caption: Glandular serous carcinoma: high N:C ratio and atypical nuclei without endometrioid features
images.credit: Soslow et al., Int J Gynecol Pathol 2019, Fig 2

images.caption: Serous endometrial intraepithelial carcinoma replacing atrophic surface epithelium (100x)

groups.heading: Clear cell carcinoma
points: Tubulocystic, papillary and solid patterns, often mixed; papillae with hyalinised, sometimes eosinophilic cores
Polygonal cells with clear or eosinophilic cytoplasm, hobnail nuclei, intraluminal eosinophilic globules
Napsin A, HNF1-beta and AMACR positive; ER and PR usually negative; p53 wild-type in most
Distinguish from: secretory endometrioid carcinoma (bland, ER positive) and Arias-Stella reaction

images.caption: Clear cell carcinoma with glandular and solid architecture (40x)
Clear cell carcinoma: tubulocystic and papillary structures lined by clear and hobnail cells
images.credit: Weiss et al., J Med Case Rep 2023, Fig 2 (H&E) (cropped)

groups.heading: Dedifferentiated carcinoma
points: Low-grade (FIGO grade 1 or 2) endometrioid carcinoma abutting an undifferentiated component, often with abrupt transition
Undifferentiated part: sheets of monotonous discohesive cells, no gland formation, often rhabdoid or myxoid areas
Loss of PAX8, ER and PR and of SWI/SNF proteins (ARID1A, ARID1B, SMARCA4) in the undifferentiated component; frequently MMR deficient
Distinguish from: FIGO grade 3 endometrioid (solid areas retain PAX8 / ER and cohesion)

images.caption: Dedifferentiated: abrupt transition between low-grade endometrioid glands and undifferentiated sheets
Dedifferentiated: FIGO grade 1 endometrioid (left) beside small, uniform, dyscohesive undifferentiated cells (right) (200x)
Dedifferentiated, rhabdoid variant: glandular component with adjacent rhabdoid undifferentiated cells (40x)

groups.heading: Undifferentiated carcinoma
points: Solid sheets of small to intermediate, monotonous, discohesive cells with no glandular or squamous differentiation
Brisk mitoses, geographic necrosis, lymphoid infiltrate; may show rhabdoid cells
Focal keratin / EMA only; PAX8, ER and PR negative; frequent SWI/SNF loss and MMR deficiency
Distinguish from: lymphoma, high-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma, neuroendocrine carcinoma, epithelioid leiomyosarcoma

images.caption: Undifferentiated: diffuse sheets of monotonous discohesive cells without gland formation (10x)
images.credit: Yang et al., Front Oncol 2025, Fig 3A (cropped)

images.caption: Undifferentiated: monomorphic round cells, SMARCA4-deficient tumour (40x)
images.credit: Yang et al., Front Oncol 2025, Fig 3B (cropped)

groups.heading: Carcinosarcoma (malignant mixed Mullerian tumor)
points: Biphasic: high-grade carcinoma (usually serous or endometrioid) and high-grade sarcoma, with sharp or intimate admixture
Homologous sarcoma: high-grade spindle cell sarcoma NOS; heterologous: rhabdomyosarcoma (eosinophilic rhabdomyoblasts), chondrosarcoma, osteosarcoma, liposarcoma
Staged and graded as a carcinoma; report the components and their proportions
Distinguish from: adenosarcoma (low-grade), endometrioid carcinoma with spindle cell areas (low grade, keratin positive), undifferentiated carcinoma

images.caption: Carcinosarcoma: malignant glands with pleomorphic rhabdoid sarcomatous cells (100x)
Homologous sarcomatous component: malignant spindle cells (400x)
Heterologous element: chondrosarcoma
Heterologous element: rhabdomyosarcoma
Heterologous rhabdomyoblasts with eccentric nuclei and eosinophilic cytoplasm (400x)
Heterologous element: osteosarcoma with osteoid (40x)
images.credit: Al Dallal et al., Front Oncol 2025, Fig 1B (cropped)

groups.heading: Mesonephric-like adenocarcinoma
points: Mixture of tubular, ductal, papillary, glomeruloid, solid and spindle patterns; small tubules with dense eosinophilic luminal secretions
Nuclei often vesicular with grooves or overlapping, resembling papillary thyroid carcinoma; mild to moderate atypia
GATA3, TTF1 (often mutually exclusive), CD10 luminal; ER and PR negative, wild-type p53; KRAS mutation
Distinguish from: endometrioid carcinoma (ER positive) and serous / clear cell carcinoma

images.caption: Mesonephric-like: papillae with delicate fibrovascular cores (200x)
Mesonephric-like: overlapping nuclei with open chromatin and grooves, thyroid-like (400x)
Mesonephric-like: irregular glands with microacinar foci (GATA3/TTF1 positive case)
images.credit: Ogunmuyiwa et al., Case Rep Obstet Gynecol 2026, Fig 3A

groups.heading: Squamous cell carcinoma, NOS
points: Pure squamous differentiation with keratinisation or intercellular bridges, no glandular component
Requires exclusion of cervical squamous carcinoma (no cervical primary, no connection) and of an endometrioid carcinoma with extensive squamous differentiation
Often arises in pyometra, cervical stenosis or ichthyosis uteri; HPV negative in most
Distinguish from: endometrioid carcinoma with squamous differentiation (any glandular element)

images.caption: Primary endometrial squamous cell carcinoma: keratinising nests (100x)
images.credit: Darré et al., J Med Case Rep 2019, Fig 2

images.caption: Primary endometrial squamous cell carcinoma infiltrating endometrium

groups.heading: Gastric (gastrointestinal)-type carcinoma
points: Glands with abundant pale or foamy mucinous cytoplasm, distinct cell borders and basal nuclei, gastric-pyloric or intestinal (goblet cell) phenotype
Deceptively bland glands may show marked cytological atypia elsewhere
MUC6, HIK1083, CDX2 or CK20 positive; ER and PR negative; frequent abnormal p53
Distinguish from: endometrioid carcinoma with mucinous differentiation (ER positive, endometrioid glands elsewhere) and metastatic gastrointestinal carcinoma

images.caption: Gastric-type mucinous carcinoma: glands with abundant pale mucinous cytoplasm (4x)
images.credit: Yang et al., Front Oncol 2025, Fig 2A (cropped)

images.caption: Gastric-type: columnar cells, basal nuclei, pale mucinous cytoplasm; CDX2/SATB2 positive (10x)
images.credit: Yang et al., Front Oncol 2025, Fig 2B (cropped)

groups.heading: Mixed cell carcinoma (specify types and percentages)
points: Two or more distinct WHO types, each recognisable on morphology (supported by IHC), each making up at least 5%
Most often endometrioid with serous or clear cell; state the types and percentages
Grade follows the highest-grade component (non-endometrioid components make the tumour high grade)
Distinguish from: a single tumour with variable architecture (e.g. serous with glandular areas)

images.caption: Mixed clear cell and endometrioid carcinoma: distinct cell shape, nuclei and growth pattern
images.credit: Murali et al., Int J Gynecol Pathol 2019, Fig 7

images.caption: Mixed neuroendocrine (left) and endometrioid (right) carcinoma with sharp demarcation (100x)

groups.heading: Small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
points: Sheets, nests and trabeculae of small cells with scant cytoplasm, fine granular chromatin, absent nucleoli and nuclear moulding
Extensive necrosis, crush artefact, brisk mitoses and apoptosis
Synaptophysin, chromogranin, CD56 or INSM1 positive (dot-like keratin); may be admixed with endometrioid carcinoma
Distinguish from: undifferentiated carcinoma, lymphoma, high-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma

images.caption: Small cell NEC: scant cytoplasm, nuclear moulding, finely granular chromatin (400x)
images.credit: Hou et al., Open Life Sci 2021, Fig 2e (cropped)

images.caption: Small cell NEC (left) merging with endometrioid glands (right): moulding, hyperchromasia, apoptosis (400x)

groups.heading: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
points: Organoid nests, trabeculae or sheets with peripheral palisading and rosettes; large cells with ample cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli
Vesicular chromatin, frequent mitoses, geographic necrosis
Diffuse neuroendocrine marker expression (synaptophysin, chromogranin, INSM1) is required; often part of a mixed tumour
Distinguish from: FIGO grade 3 endometrioid or undifferentiated carcinoma (focal, weak neuroendocrine staining does not qualify)

images.caption: Large cell NEC: organoid nests of large cells with vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli, brisk mitoses and necrosis; Syn/CgA/CD56 positive (intramyometrial uterine case)
images.credit: Yi et al., Front Oncol 2026, Fig 2A-C (cropped)

reference.title: Architectural grade: solid non-squamous growth
reference.intro: Estimate the proportion of solid growth in the non-squamous, non-morular component. Squamous morules and keratinising nests are excluded from the solid count.

groups.heading: 5% or less (architectural grade 1)
points: Well-formed, confluent back-to-back glands with little intervening stroma
Cribriform, villoglandular or papillary areas still count as glandular
Solid non-squamous sheets, if any, make up 5% or less
Distinguish from: atypical hyperplasia / EIN (no confluence, no stromal loss, no invasion)

images.caption: Grade 1: confluent glands resembling proliferative endometrium, no solid growth (40x)
Grade 1: back-to-back glands with low-grade nuclei (100x)
Grade 1 with extensive squamous differentiation: squamous areas are not counted as solid
images.credit: Soslow et al., Int J Gynecol Pathol 2019, Fig 1A (cropped)

groups.heading: 6-50% (architectural grade 2)
points: Glands remain but solid non-squamous nests or sheets form more than 5% and up to half of the tumour
Count only solid areas without gland lumina or squamous features
Grade 3 nuclei in the majority of the tumour raise this to FIGO grade 3
Distinguish from: squamous morules (bland, syncytial, often central) which do not count

images.caption: Grade 2: glands with intervening solid non-squamous nests (40x)
Grade 2: solid non-squamous growth in 6-50% of the tumour (100x)
Grade 2: <50% solid non-squamous growth
images.credit: Soslow et al., Int J Gynecol Pathol 2019, Fig 1B (cropped)

groups.heading: More than 50% (architectural grade 3)
points: Solid growth dominates; residual glands are few and often abortive
Nuclei may still be endometrioid (elongated, stratified); marked atypia throughout should prompt exclusion of serous carcinoma (p53, ER, PTEN)
Distinguish from: undifferentiated / dedifferentiated carcinoma (monotonous discohesive sheets with no gland formation, loss of PAX8 / ER)

images.caption: Grade 3: predominantly solid sheets (40x)
Grade 3: solid growth >50% (100x)
High-grade: microacinar pattern counts as solid, not glandular
images.credit: Soslow et al., Int J Gynecol Pathol 2019, Fig 1D (cropped)

reference.note: FIGO grade = architectural grade, raised by one when grade 3 nuclei occupy the majority of the tumour (WHO 5th ed).

fields.label: Nuclear grade
options: Nuclear grade 3 (marked atypia in the majority of the tumour)

is: Mixed cell carcinoma (specify types and percentages)

fields.help: Grade 3 nuclei in the majority of the tumour raise the architectural grade by one (FIGO / WHO).

reference.title: Nuclear grade
reference.intro: Assess the predominant nuclear appearance, not the worst focus. Notable nuclear atypia in the majority of the tumour raises the architectural grade by one.

groups.heading: Nuclear grade 1-2 (mild to moderate atypia)
points: Elongated, cigar-shaped or oval nuclei with even chromatin and small nucleoli
Nuclear stratification and pseudostratification within glands
Mitoses usually few to moderate
Distinguish from: reactive / secretory change with vacuoles and bland nuclei

images.caption: Nuclear grade 2: moderate enlargement, even chromatin, small nucleoli
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, single image

images.caption: Low-grade nuclei: uniform, columnar, perpendicular to the basement membrane (400x)

groups.heading: Nuclear grade 3 (marked atypia in the majority of the tumour)
points: Rounded, enlarged and pleomorphic nuclei with coarse chromatin and prominent eosinophilic nucleoli
Loss of polarity, frequent and atypical mitoses
In a glandular tumour, grade 3 nuclei throughout should prompt exclusion of serous carcinoma (abnormal p53, diffuse p16, loss of ER) before raising the grade
Distinguish from: focal bizarre nuclei in an otherwise low-grade tumour (does not upgrade)

images.caption: Grade 3 nuclei in a glandular tumour: marked pleomorphism, prominent nucleoli (raises grade 1-2 architecture by one)
images.credit: Murali et al., Int J Gynecol Pathol 2019, Fig 1B (cropped)

images.caption: Grade 3 tumour with optically clear, vesicular nuclei (100x)

is: Mixed cell carcinoma (specify types and percentages)

reference.title: Endometrioid variants and differentiation
reference.intro: Variant features do not change the type or, on their own, the grade. Recognising them prevents misdiagnosis as a non-endometrioid carcinoma.

groups.heading: Squamous differentiation
points: Morules: bland syncytial nests within gland lumina, often with central necrosis; or keratinising squamous nests and pearls
Excluded from the solid non-squamous count
Distinguish from: solid endometrioid growth (glandular nuclei, no squamous features)

images.caption: Squamous differentiation with keratin granuloma beside endometrioid glands
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, single image

images.caption: Extensive squamous differentiation in a grade 1 tumour: excluded from the solid percentage
images.credit: Soslow et al., Int J Gynecol Pathol 2019, Fig 1A (cropped)

images.caption: Grade 2 tumour with focal squamous metaplasia (40x)

groups.heading: Mucinous differentiation
points: Columnar cells with abundant intracytoplasmic mucin, often endocervical-like, in a tumour with endometrioid architecture elsewhere
ER / PR positive; wild-type p53
Distinguish from: gastric-type carcinoma (ER negative, MUC6) and endocervical adenocarcinoma

images.caption: Mucinous differentiation: intracytoplasmic and extracellular mucin, low-grade nuclei (100x)
Endocervical-type mucinous differentiation
images.credit: Buell-Gutbrod et al., Diagn Pathol 2013, Fig 1A (cropped)

images.caption: Intestinal-type mucinous differentiation with goblet cells (left: conventional endometrioid)
images.credit: Buell-Gutbrod et al., Diagn Pathol 2013, Fig 1B (cropped)

images.caption: Grade 1 endometrioid with mucinous differentiation (40x)

groups.heading: Secretory change
points: Subnuclear and supranuclear cytoplasmic vacuoles resembling early secretory endometrium
Bland nuclei, low mitotic rate; may be seen with progestogen therapy
Distinguish from: clear cell carcinoma (hobnail nuclei, hyalinised cores, Napsin A)

images.caption: Extensive secretory change: sub- and supranuclear vacuoles (100x)
Secretory change in grade 1 endometrioid carcinoma (40x)

groups.heading: Ciliated cells
points: Glands lined by cells with apical cilia and eosinophilic cytoplasm
Commonly low grade; a diagnosis of carcinoma still rests on confluent growth or invasion
Distinguish from: ciliated (tubal) metaplasia in hyperplasia

images.caption: Well-differentiated endometrioid carcinoma with abundant cilia
Diffuse ciliation of tumour cells, high power

groups.heading: Sex cord-like elements
points: Cords, trabeculae or small tubules of bland cells resembling ovarian sex cord tumour, merging with endometrioid glands
Inhibin usually negative (keratin positive), unlike true sex cord elements
Distinguish from: uterine tumour resembling ovarian sex cord tumour (UTROSCT), endometrial stromal sarcoma with sex cord elements

images.caption: Sex cord-like elements in endometrioid carcinoma (100x)
images.credit: Jia et al., Diagn Pathol 2019, Fig 2e (cropped)

images.caption: Sex cord-like cords and trabeculae (200x)
images.credit: Jia et al., Diagn Pathol 2019, Fig 2f (cropped)

groups.heading: Spindle cell (sarcomatoid) areas
points: Low-grade spindle cells merging with the glands or squamous nests, uniform nuclei, few mitoses; keratin positive
Distinguish from: carcinosarcoma (high-grade, discrete sarcoma with marked atypia and necrosis)

images.caption: Spindle cell areas merging with glands; no significant atypia in either component (200x)
Contrast: carcinosarcoma, with spatially distinct high-grade sarcomatous and carcinomatous elements (200x)

groups.heading: Corded and hyalinised (CHEC) pattern
points: Cords and single cells within hyalinised or myxoid stroma, sometimes with osteoid; merges with low-grade endometrioid glands and squamous morules
Low-grade nuclei; often nuclear beta-catenin (CTNNB1 mutation); usually young patients
Distinguish from: carcinosarcoma (high-grade components) and mixed Mullerian tumours

images.caption: CHEC: cords and small clusters in hyalinised stroma, mild to moderate atypia (100x)
images.credit: Liu et al., Front Oncol 2025, Fig 3A (cropped)

images.caption: CHEC merging with low-grade endometrioid carcinoma (40x)
images.credit: Liu et al., Front Oncol 2025, Fig 3B (cropped)

images.caption: CHEC nuclei match the conventional component (lower right) (200x)

fields.label: Histologic grade
options: Derive from the histologic type (and architecture / nuclear grade for endometrioid carcinoma)
fields.default: Derive from the histologic type (and architecture / nuclear grade for endometrioid carcinoma)
fields.help: Left on Derive, endometrioid carcinoma is graded from the solid growth and nuclear grade above and every other histotype prints as high grade (non-endometrioid); pick a value only to override.

fields.label: Pattern of myometrial invasion
options: Diffusely infiltrative single cells and cords

reference.title: Patterns of myometrial invasion
reference.intro: Measure depth from the endomyometrial junction to the deepest invasive gland. Invasion into adenomyosis is not myoinvasion; MELF is prone to being missed and mistaken for lymphovascular invasion.

groups.heading: Infiltrative glands with stromal response
points: Irregular, angulated glands or nests in myometrium with desmoplastic, oedematous or inflammatory stroma
Most common pattern; depth is usually easy to measure
Distinguish from: carcinoma in adenomyosis (endometrial stroma around the glands, rounded contour, no stromal reaction)

images.caption: Infiltrative glands: single or small groups of irregular glands scattered in myometrium
Grade 1 tumour with infiltrative myoinvasion (40x)
Myoinvasive focus of grade 3 tumour with stromal response (100x)

groups.heading: Broad pushing (expansile) front
points: Smooth, broad tumour-myometrium interface without stromal reaction; can be underestimated as no invasion
Compare with adjacent normal endomyometrial junction to gauge depth
Distinguish from: exophytic tumour compressing but not invading the myometrium

images.caption: Broad front: linear limit between tumour and underlying myometrium
Grade 1 tumour with a broad pushing front (20x)
Comparison: tumour confined to endometrium, no myoinvasion

groups.heading: MELF (microcystic, elongated and fragmented) pattern
points: Microcystic and elongated glands lined by flattened or eosinophilic, sometimes squamoid cells, fragmenting into single cells and small clusters
Fibromyxoid, inflamed stroma with neutrophils; typically at the invasive front of low-grade endometrioid carcinoma
Associated with lymphovascular invasion and lymph node micrometastasis; fragmented cells mimic histiocytes or LVSI (keratin and CD68 help)
Distinguish from: true lymphovascular invasion (endothelium-lined space, CD31 / D2-40)

images.caption: MELF: microcystic, elongated and fragmented glands at the invasive front (40x)
MELF: fibromyxoid stroma with inflammation around outpouching glands; flattened lining (200x)
MELF pattern of myoinvasion (10x)
MELF focus with stromal change and inflammatory response (100x)

groups.heading: Adenomyosis-like (irregular islands without stromal response)
points: Rounded or irregular tumour islands deep in myometrium lacking any stromal reaction and lacking endometrial stroma
Counts as invasion; depth is measured to the deepest island
Distinguish from: carcinoma colonising adenomyosis (residual endometrial stroma or benign glands at the periphery, CD10 stroma)

images.caption: Adenomyosis-like invasion: groups of malignant glands in myometrium without surrounding stroma (10x)
Adenomyosis-like: rounded groups of >5 glands simulating adenomyosis
Mimic: adenomyosis involved by carcinoma, with residual endometrial stroma and a benign gland (top right) (10x)

groups.heading: Diffusely infiltrative single cells and cords
points: Single cells, cords and small nests permeating between muscle fibres, often with minimal stromal response
May be underrecognised at low power; keratin highlights the extent
Distinguish from: MELF (microcystic glands and fibromyxoid stroma) and undifferentiated carcinoma

images.caption: Adenoma malignum-like: widely spaced, regular, low-grade glands deep in myometrium
Adenoma malignum-type invasion (20x)

snippets.label: MMR-deficient: methylation / Lynch work-up
snippets.text: The tumour shows loss of mismatch repair protein expression. Where MLH1 and PMS2 are lost, MLH1 promoter hypermethylation testing is recommended to distinguish sporadic from Lynch syndrome-associated deficiency; loss of MSH2, MSH6 or isolated PMS2, or unmethylated MLH1 loss, should prompt referral for genetic counselling and germline testing.

snippets.label: p53-abnormal: high-risk molecular group
snippets.text: The tumour is p53-abnormal on immunohistochemistry and falls within the p53-abnormal (copy-number high) molecular group, which carries an adverse prognosis independent of histotype and stage; multidisciplinary discussion of adjuvant therapy is advised.

snippets.label: POLE-mutated: favourable prognosis
snippets.text: The tumour harbours a pathogenic POLE exonuclease domain mutation and is classified as POLE-mutated (ultramutated), a group with an excellent prognosis irrespective of grade and histotype.

snippets.label: Molecular testing pending: supplementary report
snippets.text: Molecular testing is in progress; the final molecular classification will be issued as a supplementary report.

snippets.label: Multiple classifier: precedence explained
snippets.text: The tumour shows more than one molecular classifying feature (multiple classifier). By WHO and ProMisE convention a pathogenic POLE mutation takes precedence over mismatch repair deficiency, which in turn takes precedence over abnormal p53; the tumour is assigned to the group stated above.

snippets.label: Uterine and ovarian tumours: synchronous low-grade endometrioid
snippets.text: The uterine and ovarian tumours are both low-grade endometrioid carcinomas. With superficial or absent myometrial invasion, no lymphovascular space invasion and the ovarian tumour confined to the ovary, these are regarded as clonally related low-risk disease with a favourable outcome rather than as metastatic spread.

snippets.label: Peritoneal fluid cytology reported separately
snippets.text: The peritoneal washing is reported separately; please correlate.

snippets.label: Carcinosarcoma: staged as carcinoma
snippets.text: Carcinosarcoma is a biphasic tumour of metaplastic carcinoma and is staged and managed as a high-grade endometrial carcinoma; the carcinomatous and sarcomatous components, including any heterologous elements, are described above.
